line: Parliament creates the duty to use e-invoices between businesses.
subject: Germany: e-invoices between businesses become the rule from 1 January 2025
headline: UStG § 14 (Ausstellung von Rechnungen) moved to a new version, and everything we hold about it is already in force.

quotes.text: An electronic invoice is a structured electronic invoice that is issued, transmitted and received in a structured electronic format enabling electronic processing.
The structured electronic format must conform to EN 16931 or be agreed between issuer and recipient allowing correct extraction conforming to or interoperable with EN 16931.

checks: The format or syntax, and which version is in force: what your billing setup has for Germany today.
Whether a document type you still issue is permitted: what your billing setup has for Germany today.
lead: It applied 40 weeks after it was published, on 1 January 2025.

line: Law takes foreign VAT-registered businesses without a Belgian establishment out of the e-invoice duty.
subject: Belgium: who must be able to receive e-invoices changed on 20 February 2026
headline: W.Btw art. 53 moved to a new version, and everything we hold about it is already in force.

quotes.text: The recipient of a structured electronic invoice issued under § 2bis who is identified for VAT under article 50 § 1 first paragraph 1° must be able, itself or through a third party, to receive it in the format in which it was issued, and cannot invoke the customer-acceptance rule of § 2 fourth paragraph.

The supplier is not bound to issue or have issued a structured electronic invoice when the recipient is for technical reasons unable to receive it, itself or via a third party in its name and for its account.
quotes.cite: § 2bis, zesde lid, eerste zin, in force 20 February 2026

checks: Which formats have to be accepted on arrival: what your receiving setup has for Belgium today.
Acceptance and rejection states, and their deadlines: what your receiving setup has for Belgium today.
disclosure: This rests on Fisconetplus, the tax administration's copy, not the gazette, and on 20 September 2026 the amending acts it names were checked against Justel's register of amending acts and corroborated; that shows which text is in force and what amended it, not that every sentence matches the gazette word for word; reading each article against its amending act in the gazette would close the gap, a session's work per act and no money.
lead: It applied the day it was published.

line: The platform itself sends invoice, transaction and payment data to the tax administration.
subject: France: invoices between companies must go through a certified platform
headline: Code général des impôts, article 289 bis moved to a new version, and what we hold about it runs out on 1 January 2027.
when: In force since 21 February 2026, until 1 January 2027 (in 10 weeks).

quotes.text: In this later version, the option to use the government portal for invoice exchange was removed: emission, transmission and receipt of electronic invoices between French-established assujettis must go through a plateforme agréée.
quotes.cite: Article 289 bis, I, in force 21 February 2026 to 1 January 2027

quotes.text: Paragraph II, which in the earlier version routed invoicing data through the government portal to the administration, is repealed in this version.
quotes.cite: Article 289 bis, II, in force 21 February 2026 to 1 January 2027

checks: Which channel or network is mandated or forbidden: what your connection has for France today.
source: Source: Légifrance, https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000053546660. The page carries no date of its own; we saw it change on 12 October 2026.
lead: It applied the day after it was published.
subject_now: France: 1 new for you. Next date 1 January 2027.

line: Royal decree adds fines for lacking the means to send and receive e-invoices.
subject: Belgium: fines for late invoices and for not being able to e-invoice, from 1 January 2026
headline: KB nr. 44 Bijlage Afd. 2 Rubriek I was inserted, and everything we hold about it is already in force.

quotes.text: For the first failure to issue an invoice or equivalent document within the prescribed period: a fine of 50 EUR per invoice with a maximum of 500 EUR per case.
quotes.cite: KB nr. 44, Bijlage, Afdeling 2, Rubriek I, A, in force 1 January 2026

quotes.text: For the first failure to have technical means to issue and receive a structured electronic invoice: a fine of 1,500 EUR.
quotes.cite: KB nr. 44, Bijlage, Afdeling 2, Rubriek I, C, in force 1 January 2026

checks: Penalties, and the exposure they create: what your tax determination has for Belgium today.
disclosure: This rests on Fisconetplus, the tax administration's copy, not the gazette, and on 20 September 2026 the amending acts it names were checked against Justel's register of amending acts and corroborated; that shows which text is in force and what amended it, not that every sentence matches the gazette word for word; reading each article against its amending act in the gazette would close the gap, a session's work per act and no money.
lead: It applied 24 weeks after it was published, on 1 January 2026.

line: Directory must list members of a VAT group.
subject: France: the central directory now lists members of a VAT group, from 29 July 2026
headline: Code général des impôts, annexe II, articles 242 nonies B à H moved to a new version.

quotes.text: The central directory registers taxable persons subject to article 289 bis, public-law legal persons subject to electronic invoicing obligations under the public procurement code, certified platforms mentioned in article 290 B, and members of a VAT group (assujetti unique).
quotes.cite: Article 242 nonies H, I, in force 29 July 2026

checks: Which identifier must be on a record, and in what form: what your master data has for France today.

lead: It applied the day after it was published.

line: Law shortens invoice retention to eight years.
subject: Germany: keep invoices for eight years instead of ten, from 1 January 2025
headline: UStG § 14b (Aufbewahrung von Rechnungen) moved to a new version, and everything we hold about it is already in force.

quotes.text: An entrepreneur must retain an invoice copy issued by them or a third party on their behalf, and all received invoices, for eight years.

checks: Retention duration: what your archive has for Germany today.
lead: It applied 9 weeks after it was published, on 1 January 2025.
